small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose itself dominates runtime (fast_p=0.40, post-kernel is trivial). Tuning BLOCK_OC/BLOCK_HW/num_warps in fused_post_kernel will not move the needle — torch's ConvTranspose2d on (16,64,128,512,512) with k=3 is the bottleneck.
- If staying in this structure, at least try BLOCK_HW=4096 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2, and switch x to channels_last so the inner HW reduction is contiguous along the channel-major axis only if combined with kernel reindexing — otherwise leave as-is.
- Minor: precompute bias once on device with `.contiguous().view(-1)` in __init__ to avoid the reshape per forward.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), computing the outer product `x[n,ic,h,w] * w[ic,oc,kh,kw]` and atomic-adding into the (H+2, W+2) output grid. Fuse the global-mean reduction into the same kernel via a second pass that reduces directly without writing the full (N, OC, 514, 514) tensor — or accumulate per-(n,oc) sums in a workspace and skip materializing the full output.
- Better: since the downstream op only needs `mean over (H_out,W_out)` per (n,oc), write a fused ConvTranspose2d+mean kernel that still does the full multiply-accumulate count (every input element contributes to kh*kw output positions, so accumulate `sum_oc[n,oc] += x[n,ic,h,w] * w[ic,oc,kh,kw]` weighted by per-output-position validity, summed over all valid (h_out,w_out) — must enumerate every (kh,kw,h,w) pair to keep asymptotic work identical). Then a tiny epilogue does bias+logsumexp+sum*10.
- Use channels_last input layout and tile (BLOCK_IC=32, BLOCK_OC=64) GEMM-style with kh*kw as an unrolled outer loop; num_warps=8, num_stages=3. Grid: (N, ceil(OC/BLOCK_OC)).
